instructions: Implement mean_ci(values, z=1.96) returning (lower, upper): sample mean plus/minus z times the population standard deviation divided by the square root of n. Use statistics.NormalDist to sanity-check the critical value, and round the bounds to 4 decimals.

import statistics

def mean_ci(values, z=1.96):
    pass
checks_code:
lo, hi = mean_ci([12, 15, 14, 10, 12, 11, 13, 14])
assert lo == 11.5328
assert hi == 13.7172
assert lo < statistics.fmean([12, 15, 14, 10, 12, 11, 13, 14]) < hi
print("Checks passed.")
solution_code:
import math
import statistics

def mean_ci(values, z=1.96):
    n = len(values)
    mean = statistics.fmean(values)
    spread = statistics.pstdev(values) / math.sqrt(n)
    return round(mean - z * spread, 4), round(mean + z * spread, 4)

solution_code:
import hashlib

def split_indices(n, val_fraction, seed):
    keys = [(hashlib.md5(f"{seed}-{i}".encode()).hexdigest(), i) for i in range(n)]
    k = max(0, round(n * val_fraction))
    val = sorted(idx for _, idx in sorted(keys)[:k])
    val_set = set(val)
    train = [i for i in range(n) if i not in val_set]
    return train, val
